records.section_heading: Invasive didemnid tunicate spreading across coral reefs at remote Swains Island, American Samoa
records.question: What maximum relative abundances of Diplosoma similis were recorded at two sites within the major center of occurrence around Swains Island during the March 2008 surveys?
records.ground_truth_answer: Relative abundances as high as 76.5% and 35.0%.
ground_truth_chunks: Towed-diver benthic surveys, covering 28.6 ha (28.6 km · 10 m, 3.2–21.4 m depth) of forereef habitat encircling the island, confirmed widespread occurrence of the tunicate, with elevated abundance observed along the north-northwest side of the island.

Fifteen, 25-m line-point intercept survey transects (50 cm intervals at 10.9– 13.9 m depths) at eight long-term (established since 2002) monitoring stations around Swains indicated relative abundances of D. similis as high as 76.5% and 35.0% at two sites within the major center of occurrence (Fig. 1a), and between 0% and 23.5% for the remaining six sites.
